ops.title: Comparing daemonkit.Serving values with == panics at runtime — use reflect.DeepEqual
ops.body:
Found 2026-08-04 while a consumer (cc-pool statusapp) wrote a test asserting an
observer connection carries a signing requirement.

`Trust.Serving` holds its policy behind an interface, and `trust.Requirement`
carries an uncomparable field. So `==` on two `Serving` values compiles fine and
**panics at runtime**:

    comparing uncomparable type daemonkit.signedServing

Use `reflect.DeepEqual` instead. This bites any consumer comparing Serving
values — most obviously in a test asserting "this connection requires the
signed identity, and that other one still uses the same-user floor" — and the
compiler gives no warning, so it surfaces as a panic in whatever run first
exercises the comparison.

Concrete shape that hits it:

    if got.Trust.Serving != want.Trust.Serving { ... }   // panics
    if !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Trust.Serving, want) { ... } // fine

Recorded rather than fixed: daemonkit was frozen for the v0.21 flag day. If it
is ever revisited, making Serving comparable (or exposing an explicit Equal)
would remove a sharp edge that has no compile-time signal.
